clue.text: Nightmares in one having a baby

parts.note: taken as written
a cub is a young animal, a baby bear or fox
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone dreads having a child and suffers bad dreams about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are demons said to lie on sleepers, the old explanation for terrifying dreams, so the word stands for those dreams.

clue.text: Impressing claim by working model

parts.note: the claim made is 'I'm', a statement of what one is
a model at work is sitting for an artist or camera

explanation.surface: A model at work makes an impression with a bold claim.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as what a working model might say: 'I'm posing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking or grand in appearance, so making a strong impression.

clue.text: Take car to local flight line leave by coach

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Take car to local flight line leave by coach', has CAR + OCHE with 'coach' as the definition but 'Take' and 'leave by' do no job; the text looks garbled.
annotationWithheld.clue: Take car to local flight line leave by coach

clue.text: Carefully be erasing what's between Russia and the us in the main

definitions.text: what's between Russia and the us in the main

indicators.note: the letters are handled with care into a new arrangement, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Careful rubbing out of a border between two nations on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the open sea; the sea in question lies between Siberia and Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern arm of the Pacific separating Russia's far east from Alaska, part of the US.

clue.text: Guile Poe uses at the end of the book

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put to use in a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Edgar Allan Poe saves his cunning for the final pages of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uses' signals that GUILE and POE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A closing section added after the main story of a book or play.

clue.text: They fit the bill

parts.note: 'the bill' (Old Bill) is British slang for the police, so these are clothes made to fit officers

explanation.surface: Things that are exactly what is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit the bill' looks like the idiom for being suitable; read literally it means clothing that fits the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Officers' issued outfits are tailored to the police, known in Britain as the Bill.

clue.text: Loads of boys have early start

indicators.note: the boys hold the letter, signalling a container

parts.note: lads are boys

indicators.note: the start of 'early' is its first letter

explanation.surface: Lots of boys get going early.
explanation.definitionFit: To lade is to load cargo, so the word means puts loads on.

clue.text: Girl ends love affair with charm

indicators.note: the ends of the word girl are its first and last letters

parts.note: an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A girl brings a romance to a close with her charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring attractiveness, a captivating charm.

clue.text: Pass oriental drinks for a quarter

parts.note: E stands for east, the orient
a cat laps, drinks with its tongue
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An Eastern traveller has drinks for fifteen minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' looks like a quarter-hour; it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to go by or pass.

clue.text: For two pins what masked robbers wear

definitions.text: For two pins what masked robbers wear

parts.words: For two pins what masked robbers wear
parts.note: 'pins' is slang for legs, and robbers pull hosiery over their faces as masks

explanation.surface: Robbers would wear masks at the slightest excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For two pins' looks like the idiom for readily; the pins are legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosiery made of synthetic fibre, worn on the legs or pulled over a raider's head.

clue.text: Ray is in the doorway of study

indicators.note: one word is said to sit inside the other, signalling a container

parts.note: a portal is a grand doorway or entrance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Ray is standing at the entrance to someone's study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a room beside the doorway; it is the definition, in its artistic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A study is a piece of art depicting a subject, just as a portrayal depicts one.

clue.text: A wee drink before play

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky, 'wee' being Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Someone has a small whisky before going to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play written for performance on stage.

clue.text: Tick nothing for the lower part of the duet

definitions.text: the lower part of the duet

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A music teacher marks one half of a duet with no ticks at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' looks like a mark of approval; it means a moment, as in 'just a tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: In piano duets the player taking the bass part is called by this Italian term, meaning the other of two.

clue.text: Throws out gold wheels

indicators.note: one word lies outside the other, so it is put around it

parts.note: to cast is to throw
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone throws away gold wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: Small swivelling wheels fitted under furniture or trolleys.

clue.text: As born outside dumfries by necessity

parts.note: née, used before a woman's maiden name, means as born or born as

indicators.note: the outside of the word Dumfries is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A woman born on the edge of Dumfries does what she must.
explanation.walkthrough: Dumfries is a town in south-west Scotland; only its first and last letters, D and S, are used.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adverb meaning necessarily, as in the saying that one must do what one must.

clue.text: Shakes from milk producers after asking mum

indicators.note: the milk producers come after the call for silence

parts.note: 'sh' is said when asking someone to keep mum, to be quiet
udders are the glands that give a cow's milk

explanation.surface: A dairy farmer trembles at the cows after hushing their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother; it means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembles or quivers convulsively, from fear or cold.

clue.text: Time limits how to diagnose broken phones

definitions.meaning: points by which work must be done
a phone with no dial tone is said to be silent and lifeless

explanation.surface: An engineer works to a schedule repairing telephones.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: due dates for finishing a task, and telephone connections that have gone silent.

clue.text: Perseveres and bothers with repetitive strain injury

indicators.note: the bothers come with the injury inside them, signalling a container

parts.note: pests bother people

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going despite irritations and a painful wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeps going steadily despite difficulty.

clue.text: Italian food for rocky marciano

indicators.note: unsteady or broken up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: The boxer Rocky Marciano tucks into a plate of pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' looks like the boxer's first name; it signals an anagram of MARCIANO.
explanation.definitionFit: Short tube-shaped pasta, a staple of Italian cooking.

clue.text: One may get the wind up with this

definitions.text: One may get the wind up with this

parts.words: One may get the wind up with this
parts.note: 'get the wind up' sounds like becoming scared, but here air is driven into soil or water

explanation.surface: Something that makes people frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the wind up' is British idiom for take fright; read literally it is a device that puts air in.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardening tool or machine that drives air into soil or liquid.

clue.text: Doctor in beer walk

indicators.note: the doctor sits inside the beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor out for a stroll stops in a pub for a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: I got the sack about being intolerant

indicators.note: the sack goes around the other words, signalling a container

parts.note: 'the sack' is slang for bed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker fired from a job turns narrow-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got the sack' looks like being dismissed; 'the sack' is the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudiced and narrow-minded, refusing to accept other views.

clue.text: Conservatory group of admirers

definitions.meaning: a music academy where pupils are taught
a band of followers sharing one master's style

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an institution teaching music, and followers of one painter or thinker.

clue.text: Complain of Noah's craft at where to put the jaguar

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault
the ark is the boat Noah built for the animals

explanation.surface: Noah grumbles about where a jaguar can go on his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: With Noah about, 'jaguar' reads as an animal for the ark; it is the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A parking area is where a motorist leaves a vehicle such as this make of car.

clue.text: Amend — and when

definitions.meaning: here in the sense of making amends for a wrong

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: making up for a sin, and the time 'at one o'clock'.

clue.text: Compels to lie about wearing obes

indicators.note: the honours are worn around the idler, signalling a container

parts.note: OBEs are awards in the Order of the British Empire
lig is British slang for lounging about or freeloading

explanation.surface: Decorated people are made to lounge around in their medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' signals a container: the awards are worn around the idling. 'obes' is lower-case in the clue but stands for the British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to bind or force them to do something.

clue.text: Best picnic to beat

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Best picnic to beat', gives 'Best' and 'to beat' as definitions but 'picnic' has no clear job; the text looks garbled.

clue.text: Proposes moving to Minnesota

indicators.note: the letters move about, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone suggests relocating to Minnesota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like relocation; it signals an anagram of MINNESOTA.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward a candidate for a post or award.

clue.text: Gift able to work with eelgrass

indicators.note: the letters are set working into a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A present that lets someone garden with seagrass.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous giving of money or presents; a gift handed out freely.

clue.text: Digressions of a teams

parts.note: sides are the teams in a match

explanation.surface: A couple of teams wander off the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks that stray from the main subject, or words spoken apart.
